# Medical referral review


The workspace edits persistent documents and submits snapshots to a review queue.
The public API is synchronous: open(id), edit(text), close(), submit(), dispose().
Returning to a document creates a fresh editor visit and restores persisted text.
The adjacent search preview publishes after a 40 ms quiet interval; hiding it
cancels unpublished work and later queries remain usable.

The coordinator owns editor visits; the acquired confirmation capability owns a view outlet. The document repository and durable queue are separate services. Component or native source defines the local service contracts.
Their local interface contracts define the behavior to preserve.

The injected store has read/write/subscribe, the queue has enqueue/list/subscribe,
and timers have schedule(callback, delay)/cancel(handle). Render functions are
output sinks and do not call application code. Keep the workspace API and these
injected interfaces. A submission returns the queue receipt, or null when no
editor is selected. Dispose detaches integrations before closing the workspace.

Typed session coordinator and immutable receipt DTO; an acquired confirmation capability reads native visit identity.

An outlet acquires the visit active when binding is called; it cannot infer an earlier action from a receipt. Each opening creates a new identity. Native RPC only adapts timer and passive output/integration resource calls; storage, queue delivery, acquired outlet and command state execute in the target runtime.

# Public syntax/build checks
The external public evaluator parses Python/JavaScript/Vue/TypeScript source or checks Go/PHP/Ruby syntax / compiles public Java sources. These checks are required after an Action but do not test business behavior. Preserve original TASK and public README/source obligations. Independent training Oracle also applies; do not access its implementation or references. No hidden schedules or assertions are included.

public_inputs.task: The medical referral review editor currently writes on every keystroke. Coalesce edits using the trailing-task utility: after a 120 ms quiet interval write only the latest text in that editing burst. Subsequent bursts must continue to save. Preserve other supported behavior and the synchronous public interfaces. The adjacent search preview is outside this maintenance change.

limitations: This guidance applies where accepted edits must survive visit boundaries and accepted submissions retain entry-bound values; other ownership or discard policies require separate analysis.

TASK: "Preserve other supported behavior and the synchronous public interfaces. The adjacent search preview is outside this maintenance change." Preserve the shared trailing utility's preview behavior.
Exception recovery, null text semantics and ordering of simultaneously due timers are unspecified by the supplied public evidence.
Attempt 1 reports successful compilation and acceptance, but provides no behavioral observations establishing causality or cross-task effectiveness.

rules.body: Apply when editor persistence is deferred, persistence or queue delivery invokes synchronous listeners, and a submission retains its entry values while confirmation authority belongs to a particular visit. Evidence: src/Workflow.java: "Consumer<Map<String,Object>> fn=listeners.get(token); if(fn!=null) fn.accept(event);" README.md: "An outlet acquires the visit active when binding is called; it cannot infer an earlier action from a receipt. Each opening creates a new identity."

Update the accepting visit's in-memory text immediately, then push its text into a visit-owned trailing task. Keep the task usable after each completed burst. TASK: "Coalesce edits using the trailing-task utility: after a 120 ms quiet interval write only the latest text in that editing burst. Subsequent bursts must continue to save."

Consume and clear pending work before invoking persistence, so listener-enqueued edits become later work rather than being erased by completion of the old save. Preserve the existing utility's ordering: src/Workflow.java: "void flush() { if(handle!=null)env.cancel(handle); String text=pending; handle=null;pending=null; if(text!=null)work.accept(text); }"

On departure, capture the old session, revoke its current ownership, detach its captured subscription and finish old-view clearing before flushing its pending persistence. Complete that persistence before reading a replacement document. After callback-capable retirement, an outer open must recheck navigation request identity before installing its destination. README.md: "Returning to a document creates a fresh editor visit and restores persisted text."

At submit entry, capture the originating visit, its document/text snapshot and its acquired confirmation capability before flushing pending persistence. Deliver the captured snapshot afterward and return its queue receipt even if a persistence callback navigates. Evidence: src/Workflow.java: "Map<String,Object> snapshot=value(visit.id,visit.text);" README.md: "A submission returns the queue receipt, or null when no\neditor is selected."

Keep durable submission ownership separate from confirmation authority. A receipt may remain valid after navigation, but show it only while the exact acquired session remains current, including when the same document has been reopened. src/Workflow.java: "boolean active(){return owner!=null&&owner==current.get();}" Preserve nested navigation, nested edits, immutable receipts, listing copies and captured-resource cleanup. Follow the documented disposal order: README.md: "Dispose detaches integrations before closing the workspace."

A guard on final destination installation alone does not protect against stale clearing after a persistence callback. Binding confirmation after flushing also cannot recover the entry visit from receipt contents. Do not discard pending edits merely because their visit departs, and do not import accepted-command retention into contracts that revoke commands on navigation.

Check no writes before the quiet deadline, one latest-value write per burst and successful later bursts. Exercise open, close and dispose with pending edits, then reopen the document. Navigate, reopen the same document and enqueue edits inside store and queue listeners. Independently check persisted text, accepted snapshot and receipt count, returned receipt, current document output, subscription ownership and confirmation suppression. Verify that callback-enqueued edits save later and that preview timing, hide cancellation and later-query usability remain preserved.

checkpoints: Before 120 ms of quiet, edits update the selected session's text without writing each keystroke.
At the quiet-interval deadline, persist only the latest text from that burst; a later burst can schedule and complete another save.
On open or close, persist the departing visit's pending text so returning to the document restores it.
On submit, bind the visit, snapshot and confirmation capability before callback-capable persistence; persist accepted edits before queue delivery.
During synchronous store or queue callbacks, verify that nested navigation and edits retain their own ownership and state.
Verify that preview timing, hide cancellation and later-query usability remain unchanged.
forbidden_effects: Continuing to write on every keystroke.
Losing pending accepted edits when a visit closes or another document opens.
Allowing an old visit's pending save to overwrite a later visit's newer persisted edits.
Letting an outer operation overwrite a visit installed by synchronous callback navigation.
Changing an accepted submission's document or text because a callback navigates or edits.
Showing a submission confirmation in a different editor visit, including a later visit to the same document.
Changing the adjacent search preview's behavior or the synchronous public interfaces.
lifecycle_identity: Each opening creates a distinct Session identity, even when reopening the same document ID.
Pending editor persistence belongs to the Session and document that accepted the edits.
A submission snapshot belongs to the visit and text captured at submit entry.
Confirmation authority uses Session object identity, not document ID or receipt contents.
Navigation identity must distinguish an outer open from navigation performed by synchronous callbacks.

obligations.text: Use the existing trailing-task utility to coalesce editor edits: after 120 ms without another edit, write only the latest text in the burst.
Keep the session's in-memory text current immediately, and preserve the ability to save subsequent editing bursts after a prior trailing save completes.

Preserve accepted edits across open, close and dispose. Complete a departing visit's pending persistence before a replacement visit reads persisted text, while protecting navigation performed by persistence callbacks.

Preserve submission behavior: return null with no selected editor; otherwise capture one entry-bound document/text snapshot, make its pending edits durable before queue delivery, return the queue receipt and keep callback-enqueued edits as later work.
Acquire confirmation authority for the entry visit before callback-capable work. Publish the receipt only while that exact visit remains current.
Preserve synchronous listener delivery, receipt immutability, queue listing copies, subscription cleanup, output behavior and the documented disposal order.
Keep the public workspace and injected interfaces synchronous and unchanged. Leave the adjacent search preview outside the maintenance change.

Finish pending departure persistence before reading the replacement document's stored text.
Capture submission identity, text and confirmation authority before flushing pending persistence; deliver the captured snapshot to the queue afterward.
Preserve the documented requirement that disposal detaches integrations before closing the workspace.

Store writes notify subscribed listeners synchronously, so persistence is a reentrancy boundary.
Queue capture records an immutable receipt before synchronously notifying listeners.
Nested navigation remains authoritative, and cleanup acts on captured departing resources.
Returning to a document creates a fresh visit and restores persisted text.
Search preview retains its 40 ms trailing publication and cancellation behavior.

change_summary: Merge navigation ownership and accepted-entry binding guidance into a deferred-persistence lifecycle.
Add explicit consumption-before-callback and departure-save-before-replacement-read barriers.

reflection_update.reason: The primary lineage, editor-navigation-reentry, supplies retirement and navigation protection; accepted-entry-binding supplies snapshot retention and separation of accepted work from current-view effects. Their complementary rules meet at the newly introduced persistence callback boundary. The public task and source support the added ordering checkpoints; the automatic Contract is not used as normative evidence. Attempt 1 implements these checkpoints and reports acceptance, with no reported failure to attribute. This is a source-supported guidance refinement, not evidence that prior guidance caused a failure.

limitations: Content acceptance does not establish cross-task effectiveness.

rules.body: Saving or subscription cleanup synchronously calls host listeners that may open another document or close the workspace.

Capture the old view and remove its current ownership. Finish final old-view effects, such as clearing its display, before callback-capable saving, or check authority for effects remaining after callbacks. An outer open rechecks its request identity after retirement.
Nested open/close, nested editing and the new view's rendering remain authoritative. Disposal also cleans up captured resources rather than clearing objects installed by a callback.
Protecting only final view installation can still leave a later stale clearing render. Do not require every host to detach first; notification order follows the current contract.

Invoke open/close inside listeners for timer-driven and departure-driven saves. Check document output, subscriptions and nested edits after the outer call returns, through both direct calls and actual unmounting.

limitations: Content acceptance does not establish cross-task effectiveness.

rules.body: One startup may emit multiple packets synchronously. Handling the first may hide the panel or open another visit before startup returns physical cleanup capability.
Check the originating visit and attempt before each packet enters decoding. Retirement immediately revokes later admission without waiting for physical listener removal.
Previously admitted packets settle under their separate audit and display contracts. The new visit receives bootstrap and later updates normally.
Zero listeners after cleanup does not establish correctness during startup. Do not confuse previously admitted work with packets arriving after retirement.

Hide, switch and reopen the same source from the first synchronous callback. Emit more packets before outer startup returns, and independently check rejection of new packets and settlement of admitted packets.

limitations: Content acceptance does not establish cross-task effectiveness.

rules.body: Startup, cleanup, saving or publication can synchronously reenter navigation and install a new owner.

Capture old resources and publish retirement before callback-capable work. Establish provisional cleanup ownership before startup where needed. After callbacks, recheck request and owner identity before installing a returned handle or publishing a destination.
Complete cleanup for captured old resources without clearing or taking ownership of a newer visit. Preserve the documented idempotent cleanup behavior.
Do not assume code after a synchronous callback still owns the current view. Do not hard-code one cleanup ordering when the current API requires a different order; guard remaining effects.
Exercise hide, switch and dispose inside startup, detachment and saving; check both resulting view and resource ownership after the outer call returns.

limitations: Content acceptance does not establish cross-task effectiveness.

rules.body: The current contract accepts one command for the originating visit at retry entry. Retry replaces a physical attempt without opening a new visit.

Capture the originating visit, file and record ownership. Preserve the accepted command and entry-bound record even if cancellation navigates. Independently determine whether the new attempt may attach to the current visit.
Preserve command cardinality, queue records, return values, cancellation notices and the new visit's resources. Do not redirect record ownership to the selection established by a callback.
Navigation does not universally require retry to continue. If the target contract revokes the command, follow that policy rather than importing historical retention.
Switch or hide during cancellation. Check exactly one entry-bound command, its original record ownership, cancellation of invalid handles and protection of the new visit.

limitations: Content acceptance does not establish cross-task effectiveness.

rules.body: The current contract accepts a command at entry and requires its result or record to retain that entry document, visit, attempt or text across synchronous callbacks.

Capture the accepted identity and required values at entry. Preserve that command and its entry-bound record across callbacks while independently checking whether UI or physical resources may attach to the current visit.
Preserve accepted-work cardinality, return values and record shape. Treat callback-enqueued edits as later work.
Navigation does not universally require continuing retry or submission. If the current contract revokes the command, follow that policy; do not import the source cases' retention policy.
Navigate or edit inside cancellation, persistence and record callbacks. Check the accepted command's identity, count and returned result separately from current-view effects.
